newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan minister takes hard line on MOF deposit rate.
newsitem.headline: Japan minister takes hard line on MOF deposit rate.

text.p: Japan's Health and Welfare Ministry, led by its feisty minister Junichiro Koizumi, said on Wednesday that it would not accept lower interest rates paid on its deposits held at the Ministry of Finance (MOF).
"Even if MOF asks us for a cut in the rate, I will not accept it. It's a matter at the core of Japan's fiscal investment and loan program (FILP)," Koizumi told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday.

The MOF has been pushing to cut the rate, which has not changed since January despite a recent fall in the issue rate on 10-year Japanese government bonds, on which the deposit rate is customarily set.
The deposit rate has been at a record-low 2.9 percent since January.
Koizumi's hard-line stance reflects his long-standing protest against the FILP, which is managed by MOF's Trust Fund Bureau, a Welfare Ministry spokesman said.
He did not say what the ministry would do if MOF went ahead and cut the rate. In the past, the ministry has never opposed a rate cut.

FILP has been dubbed Japan's second national budget, because it uses deposits made by the Welfare and Posts and Telecommunications ministries to fund government-affiliated financial institutions and other quasi-governmental bodies.
The balance sheet of many of those entities show big deficits.
Koizumi has charged that the system should either be stopped or revamped because the government bodies are inefficient and poorly managed.
"Money belonging to the people in the form of pension, postal savings and postal life insurance is not being used effectively under the present FILP," Koizumi said.

Analysts said that a refusal by the Welfare Ministry to accept a planned cut in the deposit rate would likely further worsen the balance sheets of government-affiliated financial institutions and quasi-governmental bodies and lead to a fundamental review of the FILP system.
Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Tuesday that he is ready to discuss the issue with Koizumi.
Koizumi has said his ministry ultimately wants to stop making deposits at MOF as he doubts the efficiency of the FILP system.
